title: IT / Finance / Security Weekly Ops Sync
summary: Weekly coordination between IT, Finance Ops, Security and Legal to align on vendor onboarding (KMS/HSM questions), upcoming procurement for dedicated capacity hardware, patching window for infra, and audit evidence needs for SOC2 prep. Agreed next steps around pricing review, security questionnaire follow-up, and scheduling a pilot benchmark with Platform Ops.

Patch window scheduling and rollback plan

transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2025-02-12
Start time: 10:00 PST
Duration: ~45 minutes
Attendees: Maya Chen, Luis Ortega, Priya Nair, Alex Romero, Ellen Park, Dana Li (CFO), Tom Baxter, Rajiv Singh

[00:00] Maya: Okay folks, thanks for joining. I think we can get started. Quick check — agenda in the shared doc, anything to add?
[00:17] Luis: No, I think the procurement timeline is the big one for finance, also the cost model for Dedicated GPUs.
[00:25] Priya: And from security we'll need the KMS / HSM answers plus vendor questionnaire — a few items were outstanding.
[00:34] Maya: Right, I'll pull up the shared vendor notes. (rustle) Um, quick house-keeping: recorded for notes.
[00:45] Alex: Great. Legal just needs visibility on SLAs and data residency clauses before we go live with any vendor.
[00:52] Ellen: Platform Ops wants a pilot window — two, maybe three days of benchmarks — to validate latency targets and KV cache behaviour.
[01:05] Dana (CFO): From finance side we also want to see committed pricing versus burst pricing; need monthly run-rate scenarios.
[01:12] Maya: Okay, let's go topic by topic. First: KMS/HSM. Priya?
[01:20] Priya: Sure. We got back a high-level note from Vendor A but it's light on key rotation and multi-tenant key separation. The vendor says they support external KMS via standard APIs but the doc uses 'KMS' generically and sometimes writes K-M-S as dashes so it looked auto-merged.
[01:38] Priya: We asked for diagrams showing where keys live for Dedicated vs Hosted variants; haven't received the detailed architecture yet. Need explicit confirmation that customer keys stay in our tenant and are not shared.
[01:49] Tom: For procurement we need a checklist of must-haves. If keys are handled in vendor-managed HSM, CFO will flag that unless there's a contract clause on exclusivity.
[02:02] Alex: Legal note: if it's vendor-managed HSM, we need vendor audit evidence (SOC2 or ISO) and KMS access controls, plus right-to-audit clauses.
[02:14] Priya: Also need an answer on BYOK (bring-your-own-key) support — whether the vendor rotates, whether we can rotate on demand. They mentioned rotation but it's unclear if it's customer-initiated.
[02:26] Maya: Action then: Priya to follow up for architecture diagrams and BYOK/rotation semantics. Add that to action items.
[02:33] Priya: Yep. I'll ping them today, ask for diagrams and the rotation API endpoints.
[02:40] (crosstalk)
[02:45] Maya: Next, procurement timeline and cost modelling — Luis?
[02:50] Luis: Finance has put together a template; I'm going to include 3 vendor scenarios: Vendor A (lower unit cost but higher network egress), Vendor B (higher up-front commit discounts), Vendor C (open-source-driven provider with lower support). Need to plug in expected Q3 usage — we're estimating 50M tokens/month for the pilot bucket.
[03:12] Dana: Quick interrupt — 50M tokens is fine as a pilot but we need monthly run-rate numbers for 6/12 months to show budget owners.
[03:22] Luis: Yep, will do 1/3/6/12 month slices. Also will include committed vs on-demand pricing and a sensitivity on latency SLA penalties.
[03:33] Rajiv: For engineering, the burst vs sustained throughput matters — if we get a vendor that only scales poorly, we'll pay more. Need to understand autoscale policies and dedupe with our smart routing.
[03:44] Ellen: For Platform Ops, can we also capture whether vendors support dedicated GPU pools in the same region? That's a must for latency.
[03:53] Luis: I'll add regional pricing differentials.
[03:57] Maya: Cool. Next: patching window. Ellen, what's the plan?
[04:03] Ellen: We're proposing a monthly maintenance window, Sunday 02:00-05:00 PST, with a 30-minute rollback test beforehand. We need an agreed outage policy in case a patch impacts running KV caches or the serving runtime.
[04:18] Priya: Security request: patching notes need to include canary and rollback steps and a list of services that must remain hot. We can't have all caches flushed without notice.
[04:28] Ellen: Understood. For Dedicated pools we will schedule rolling restarts; KV cache warmup time is about 12-15 minutes per host in current tests.
[04:38] Rajiv: That 12-15 minutes matters for user latency; Platform should surface estimated impact.
[04:44] Maya: Action: Ellen to share patch runbook, include rollback plan.
[04:49] Ellen: I'll share the doc by EOD today.
[04:54] (short pause)
[05:02] Maya: SOC2 prep — Alex, quick status?
[05:06] Alex: We're compiling evidence for the upcoming audit. Missing items: vendor contracts showing encryption, KMS logs retention, and incident response runbooks. We also need a printed list of who has key access.
[05:20] Priya: We can supply an access matrix; but we need the vendor to provide key access logs or a method to export audit events. Not all vendors support that.
[05:30] Alex: For procurement, include required evidence fields in the RFP — KMS logs, SSO integration, RBAC controls, and data residency info.
[05:39] Luis: I'll add those to the procurement checklists.
[05:43] Maya: Can we get an approximate timeline for the audit readiness?
[05:47] Alex: If we collect all evidence by end of March, the auditor can start in mid-April. So procurement needs to align so we onboard before then or have compensating controls documented.
[06:00] Dana: Budget-wise, if we need extra consulting for SOC remediation that will be a separate line item.
[06:07] Maya: Noted. Next: pilot benchmark — Ellen?
[06:10] Ellen: Proposed pilot: two 8-hour runs, one steady-state low-latency profile and one bursty request pattern to exercise batching and KV caches. We'll need a reserved small Dedicated pool for the runs — maybe 4 GPUs, ideally the vendor's nearest region.
[06:26] Rajiv: Also want to validate the kernel selection behaviour on long sequences, to ensure no regressions vs our internal estimator.
[06:35] Ellen: We'll include sequence-length profiles in the test harness.
[06:38] Maya: Scheduling constraints?
[06:40] Ellen: Prefer weekdays but vendor availability might push it to weekend. We need two contiguous days.
[06:45] Luis: Cost estimate for pilot?
[06:47] Ellen: Roughly $6k-$10k depending on vendor commit. I'll get firm numbers.
[06:54] Maya: Action: Maya to schedule pilot with Platform Ops and confirm resource estimate.
[06:59] Maya: Anything else on pilot?
[07:02] (silence)
[07:05] Maya: Okay, vendor questionnaire — status? Priya?
[07:08] Priya: We received Vendor A's security questionnaire but several answers are vague. For example, their incident response answer references a "standard playbook" without versioning. We need specifics: RTO, RPO, contact matrix.
[07:21] Tom: Procurement wants the vendor to include a point-of-contact for security incidents and a committed SLA for response times.
[07:29] Alex: Legal will add contractual language for incident notification timelines that map to our own IR process.
[07:35] Priya: I'll mark the questionnaire items that require more specifics and send back a follow-up.
[07:40] Maya: Good. AOB — any blockers?
[07:44] Dana: Budget approval pending the cost model, otherwise no blockers.
[07:49] Luis: I will push the cost model to the shared drive later today.
[07:53] Rajiv: For engineering, we need vendor API docs early — 2 weeks before pilot — to wire up routing and auth.
[08:03] Maya: Action: Luis to include API doc deadlines in the procurement calendar.
[08:09] Priya: One more point: retention policies for logs — we need to map vendor retention to our retention policy, especially for keys and audit logs.
[08:20] Alex: Legal will add data retention clauses to the contract template.
[08:24] Maya: Ok let's recap next steps. Luis will circulate procurement calendar and TCO scenarios; Priya will chase KMS diagrams and questionnaire; Maya will schedule pilot and run baseline; Alex will draft legal timeline; Ellen will share patch runbook.
[08:40] Tom: Can we get a quick follow-up meeting mid-next-week to validate the procurement list?
[08:46] Maya: Yes — propose Wednesday 2025-02-19 10am PT, I'll send the invite.
[08:53] (end recap)
[09:00] Maya: Thanks everyone, meeting adjourned.

Notes on transcription quality: some vendor/product names mangled (e.g., "CloudVendorX" transcribed as "Cloud V Co" in parts), timestamps approximate.
